# Golden fixtures

Generated by `cargo test -p tmgr-chat-relay --test fixtures -- --ignored write_fixtures` from fixed keys
(secret bytes are repeated single bytes) and fixed entropy. `fixtures_are_current` fails if a file differs
by one byte. Spec: `docs/plans/2026-11-21-tm-1017-e2e-relay.md` v1.3 sections 2-3.

Every file except `trust.json` is `{description, inputs, outputs}`. A TS port feeds `inputs` to its own
implementation and must reproduce `outputs` byte for byte. Hex fields end in `_hex`, public keys are base64
STANDARD padded, secrets are test keys only.

- `chat.json`, `blob.json`: inputs are `user_id`, `now_ms`, `sender`/`recipient` (`device_id`, `keys`),
  `kind`, `msg_id`, `sent_at_ms`, `seq`, `payload`, `entropy` (`eph_secret_hex`, `nonce_hex`).
  Outputs: `ctx`, `inner` (exact string that is hashed and signed), `inner_sha256_hex`, `signed_string`, `sig`
  (ECDSA is deterministic, DER low-S), `plaintext` (padded to 1024 bytes, `plaintext_len`), `body` (padded),
  `plaintext_unpadded`, `body_unpadded`, and `open` (the expected result of opening `body` at `now_ms`; also
  valid for `body_unpadded`). `keys` holds `sign_secret_hex`, `kex_secret_hex`, `sign_pub`, `kex_pub`, `fp`.
- `intro.json`: inputs `user_id`, `introducer`, `target` (with `kind`), `issued_at_ms`; outputs `statement`,
  `sig`, `intro_json`.
- `intro_v2.json`: inputs `user_id`, `introducer` (with `kind`), `target` (with `kind`), `issued_at_ms`; outputs `intro` and
  `self_intro`, each `{statement, sig, intro_json}`. Statement tag `tmgr-chat-intro:v2:`, envelope `"v":2`, signed exactly
  like v1. The self-intro has the introducer as target (same id and fp, kind = its own kind); it is only the upgrade marker
  and its kind is never taken. A v2 statement re-tagged as v1 must fail verification.
- `join_v2.json`: same shape as `join.json`. The code is `tmgr-chat-join:v2:` + base64url JSON
  `{"v":2,"user_id","device_id","fp","kind","secret","exp"}` (`kind` = the approver's kind, desktop or mobile) and the MAC
  transcript starts `tmgr-chat-join:v2:`; v2 and v1 MACs of the same fields differ.
- `revoke.json`: inputs `user_id`, `revoker`, `target`, `issued_at_ms`; outputs `statement`, `sig`,
  `revoke_json` (the string for `POST /revocations`).
- `join.json`: inputs `code` (`secret_hex` is the MAC key, `secret_b64` is what the code carries) and `joiner`;
  outputs `code_string`, `code_base64url`, `mac_transcript`, `mac_hex`.
- `spawnkey.json`: inputs `user_id`, `device`, `spawn_secret_hex`, `spawn_pub`, `issued_at_ms`; outputs
  `statement`, `sig`, `spawn_sig`, `payload`.
- `unicode.json`: `chat` (same shape as `chat.json`, non-ASCII payload) and `join` (same shape as `join.json`,
  non-ASCII label; the label hash is over its UTF-8 bytes).
- `trust.json`: top-level `user_id` (the user the set is computed for) and `cases[]`, each
  `{name, note, inputs: {pins, revoked [fp], intros [intro_json], directory [{device_id, sign_pub, kex_pub}]},
  outputs: {trusted, mismatches}}`. `pins` and `trusted` are `{device_id, fp, sign_pub, kex_pub}` sorted by
  (device_id, fp). `mismatches` is `{device_id, pinned_fp, directory_fp}` for trusted ids whose directory keys
  give another fp (the UI must alert; the pinned keys stay in use). `intros` is the union of directory and
  locally cached intros. Rules the cases pin down: intros verify only against the pinned keys of a trusted
  introducer matched on `(by, introducer_fp)`; the statement `user_id` must equal the user; a new entry takes
  its keys from the directory entry of that id and only if their fp equals the intro's `N_fp`; a revoked fp never
  re-enters, even under a new id.
- `trust_v2.json`: top-level `user_id` and `cases[]`, each `{name, note, inputs, outputs, same_outputs_as?}`.
  Run every case through the kind-aware trust evaluation (`trusted_set_by_kind`) and compare; when
  `same_outputs_as` names another case, the two `outputs` must be equal (order independence, runner wins in both
  orders). All lists in `outputs` are compared after sorting.
  - `inputs.devices[]`: `{name, device_id, keys}` (same `keys` object as the other files, secrets included;
    only the public parts and `fp` are needed). Keys such as `own`, `roots`, `known` use `"{device_id}:{fp}"`.
  - `inputs.own`: key of the evaluating device, or `null`. It never blocks the runner gate and never takes a kind.
  - `inputs.start[]`: starting pins `{device_id, fp, sign_pub, kex_pub}` (the pins on a normal sync, the base
    roots on a revoke).
  - `inputs.roots[]`: base roots. A root without an entry in `known` is assumed to be `desktop` for vouching only;
    that stand-in is never returned as a kind, never conflicts and never counts as an existing value.
  - `inputs.known`: map key to kind (`desktop|mobile|runner`), the kinds stored before the run.
  - `inputs.revoked[]`: revoked fps. `inputs.max_passes`: pass cap, `null` means `2 * n + 1` where `n` counts
    the distinct keys in `known`, `start` and intro targets.
  - `inputs.intros[]`: intro JSON strings (v1 and v2) in the given order, `inputs.directory[]`:
    `{device_id, sign_pub, kex_pub}`.
  - `inputs.revoke_from_base`: `null`, or `{trusted_before: [key]}`. When set, the result of the run is restricted:
    `trusted` keeps only keys in `trusted_before`, and `kinds` keeps only entries whose key has a value in `known`
    and whose new value is `runner` (revoke may only drop trust and lower kinds).
  - `outputs.trusted[]`: `{device_id, fp}`. `outputs.kinds[]`: `{device_id, fp, kind}`, kinds learned by the run
    for trusted keys only (value differs from `known`, assumed roots excluded). `outputs.conflicts[]`:
    `{device_id, fp}` of the final pass. `outputs.unstable[]`: device ids (set semantics). `outputs.passes`: count.
  - Algorithm the cases pin down: each pass starts from `known` (plus assumed roots) with the `lowered` set
    (keys demoted to `runner` so far) applied and the kinds `raised` by the previous pass; only counted v2
    intros of trusted signers that may vouch give candidates (self-intros give none; v1 intros count only for a
    target with a known `desktop`/`mobile` kind and only while the runner gate is closed). Merge per key: any
    `runner` claim wins; desktop vs mobile keeps the existing value; a tie with no existing value stays unknown;
    each disagreement is a conflict. New `runner` results go into `lowered` and clear `raised`, then the pass
    reruns; a change in `raised` also reruns. Only the final pass counts. At the cap the result is `unstable`,
    trusted keeps only `own`, and no kinds are returned.
- `negative.json`: `context` (user, now, default msg id, recipient and sender), `message_vectors[]` and
  `intro_vectors[]`. A message vector is opened with the recipient keys and the sender pinned (not pinned when
  `sender_trusted` is false; then the sender's directory keys are offered, which only `join` accepts). Optional
  per-vector overrides: `user_id`, `now_ms`, `msg_id`. `expect` is `{error: code}` (codes are `tmgr-phone`
  `Error::code()`: `bad_json`, `bad_format`, `open_failed`, `bad_key`, `bad_window`, `id_mismatch`) or
  `{ok: {seq, trusted}}`. An intro vector is `verify_intro(intro_json, user_id, signer.device_id,
  signer.sign_pub, signer.kex_pub)`. The 10-minute freshness rule for runner input is not part of this crate and
  has no vector; the 31-day `sent_at` window edges (past and future) do.

## Unknown fields

Unknown JSON fields are ignored everywhere (body, plaintext, inner, intro, revoke, API responses), so
later versions can add fields. Duplicate keys are never ignored: they are rejected.

## Notes for the JS port

- `@noble` p256: verify with `lowS: false` (high-S signatures must be accepted), DER only: a raw 64-byte r||s
  signature is rejected; emit DER low-S.
- Use a strict JSON parser that rejects duplicate keys at any depth (body, plaintext, inner, payload) and
  rejects lone surrogate escapes.
- Check base64 by re-encoding: decode, encode again, and require the exact original string (padded, canonical).
- Senders call `toWellFormed()` on every string they put into JSON so no lone surrogate is ever produced.
- Integers (`user_id`, `sent_at`, `seq`, `issued_at_ms`, `exp`) must be plain digits: no exponent, fraction,
  sign or leading zeros, in statements and in JSON.
- `inner` is hashed and signed as the exact received string; parse it only to read `sent_at`, then verify, and
  never re-serialise.
